attachments.origin_landmark: external (gluteal) surface of the ilium between the anterior and inferior gluteal lines

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Deepest of the 3 gluteal abductors, functionally paired with gluteus medius as a primary hip abductor/pelvic stabilizer during single-leg stance.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

trigger_points.location_description: Anterior portion of the muscle fibers
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Pain and tenderness to the lower lateral buttock, the lateral aspect of the thigh and knee, and the peroneal region of the leg as far as the ankle
trigger_points.notes: Travell named this the 'pseudo-sciatica' muscle because this extensive leg referral can closely mimic true sciatic radiculopathy; distinguishing features are a dull, achy quality (versus a sharp/electric quality) and normal neurologic exam
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual (Travell JG, Simons DG, Simons LS, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 2: The Lower Extremities, 1st ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1992; Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019) -- as cited in painfreehealth.ca, 'Gluteus Minimus Muscle' clinical page, describing separate anterior-fiber and posterior-fiber referral zones (the 'pseudo-sciatica' pattern Travell named this muscle for); corroborated by real clinical evidence: Skorupska E, Dybek T, Rychlik M, Jokiel M, Zawadzinski J, Dobrakowski P (2021) 'Amplified Vasodilatation within the Referred Pain Zone of Trigger Points Is Characteristic of Gluteal Syndrome-A Type of Nociplastic Pain Mimicking Sciatica.' J Clin Med 10(21):5146, doi:10.3390/jcm10215146 (https://doi.org/10.3390/jcm10215146) -- retrieved via PubMed

trigger_points.location_description: Posterior portion of the muscle fibers
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Pain referred to the lower lateral buttock down the lateral and posterior aspect of the thigh and calf
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Walking and weight-bearing on an uneven surface, prolonged standing, and a Trendelenburg-type gait pattern
